rationale: Interpret the retained receipt of the first experiment (execution d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, both generated cases passed) against the source-based account, correct the two recorded knowledge citations whose line intervals no longer match the declared source ranges (state.go has 174 lines; installSnapshot starts at 1837), refresh the question's discriminator, and submit the successor experiment: the receipt's raw ca_setup/ca_probe events carry exactly the values the five declared predicates test, but every comparison resolved unknown because ca_setup omitted the mode field `tag` that the prerequisite alias conditions select on, so the admission event could not be associated ('Missing operation admission fields or identity', 'Ambiguous prerequisite association; missing trimmed_setup.tag'). knowledge.statement: The InstallSnapshot handler does not update the receiving node's cached last log entry (lastLogIndex/lastLogTerm). It sets lastApplied and lastSnapshot to the request's LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm, replaces the committed and latest configurations, and then either deletes the whole log store (monotonic store) or calls compactLogs, which trims only up to min(snapshotIndex, cachedLastLogIndex - TrailingLogs).
knowledge.conditions: Reached by a follower for an accepted snapshot request in the installSnapshot declaration cited as src_install_snapshot_tail (raft.go 1837-1977; the lastApplied/lastSnapshot/configuration/compaction tail at raft.go 1952-1977); compaction rules cited as src_compaction (snapshot.go 217-279); cache accessors cited as src_get_last_entry (state.go 160-174).
knowledge.changed_premise: Citation correction only: the recorded conditions named the interval raft.go 1930-1977 and state.go 160-175, but the declared source range for installSnapshot covers raft.go 1837-1977 and state.go ends at line 174. The behavior claim is unchanged.

knowledge.statement: getLastEntry returns (lastLogIndex,lastLogTerm) whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex, and the snapshot's (index,term) only when the cached log index is strictly below the snapshot index. A follower whose cached log index is at or above the newly installed snapshot index therefore keeps reporting its pre-snapshot log tail as its last entry, both for prev-log verification of incoming AppendEntries and for the log-completeness test used when granting votes or pre-votes.
knowledge.conditions: src_get_last_entry (state.go 160-174); consumers: src_append_prev_check (raft.go 1458-1606, prev-log verification at 1490-1516), src_vote_log_check (raft.go 1725-1748), and the AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog initialiser in the same handler.

investigations.discriminator: Successor run of the same two-case experiment with the admission event fixed (ca_setup now carries tag): the resolved outcomes of repeated_snapshot_installs, victim_not_caught_up and stale_claim_persists in the trimmed case plus their negations in the untrimmed control. A trimmed-case observation in which the follower catches up, or a control observation in which a snapshot is re-installed, would change the judgment; the source-side vote consequence stays unmeasured until an election is induced while a node holds such a claim.

interpretations.rationale: Present conclusion: in this revision a follower that accepts an InstallSnapshot whose index is not above its own cached last log index is left advertising a log it no longer holds and cannot accept any further log entry from that leader, so the cluster keeps re-shipping the same snapshot while the follower's applied state stays at the snapshot index. Basis, source side: installSnapshot sets lastApplied, lastSnapshot and the configurations but never lastLog (src_install_snapshot_tail), getLastEntry prefers the cached log tail whenever lastLogIndex >= lastSnapshotIndex (src_get_last_entry), the non-monotonic compaction path cannot remove a suffix that still lies above the snapshot index (src_compaction), every prev-log check then misses or mismatches so the leader only decrements nextIndex one step at a time (src_replicate_failure) until setupAppendEntries reports ErrLogNotFound and the leader re-sends the newest snapshot, after which nextIndex is reset to snapshotIndex+1 (src_send_snapshot_result). Basis, retained receipt (execution d1897256143f4de2b0477a3460ae392b, exit 0, both generated cases passed): in the trimmed case the setup event (index 0) recorded the victim's cached last log claim (index 95, term 2) with the leader's snapshot at index 83/term 3, its store 1-95 intact and zero restores; after reconnecting, the probe event (index 14) recorded the victim's FSM restored 4 -> 1193 times inside the 3s window with the leader's snapshot index still 83 (leader_snapshot_is_unchanged true), the victim's applied index unchanged at 83 while the cluster frontier reached 95 with new entries committed and applied elsewhere, the cached claim still (index 95, term 2) with the store suffix 84-95 kept, the victim's commit index still 0, and exactly one stable leader set over the window. The untrimmed control on the same history (setup index 15, probe index 29) accepted no snapshot at all (restores 0, repeated_snapshot_installs false), repaired the claim with entries (index 95, term 3) and caught up (applied 83 -> 95, commit 95), which excludes the mere existence of the stale suffix as the cause. The five declared comparisons resolved unknown, not holds: the admission event ca_setup carried no tag field, so the trimmed_setup/untrimmed_setup alias conditions could not be evaluated and the admission could not be associated ('Missing operation admission fields or identity', 'Ambiguous prerequisite association; missing trimmed_setup.tag'); the successor experiment fixes exactly that field. The raw retained values therefore support the account, but the comparison-level verdict, and with it the formal conclusion, is still pending. Limits: three voters, in-memory log store with a file snapshot store, TrailingLogs=10, a restarted ex-leader whose orphan suffix came from applies it accepted while partitioned, a 3s idle-plus-steady-writes window, and a single induced full partition; the vote-side consequence of the stale claim (knowledge-1) never triggered because no election occurred, the monotonic-store variant deletes the suffix instead of keeping it and needs its own receipt, and nothing here measures whether the state persists beyond the window or whether a larger cluster with several trimmed voters could still repair the node.
counterevidence: The untrimmed control accepted no snapshot, repaired the stale suffix with ordinary log entries and reached the cluster frontier, so a stale log suffix by itself does not stall replication; the trimmed leader log plus the install path is the trigger.

The successful InstallSnapshot refreshes the follower's last contact, so the follower never campaigned: the receipt shows one stable leader set over the whole window and the victim's term fixed at 3, so the starved state is stable rather than self-healing in this configuration.
The five declared comparisons are recorded as unknown because the admission event omitted the mode field the alias conditions test; no completed comparison verdict exists yet for this question.
limitations: Measured configuration only: three voters, InmemStore plus FileSnapshotStore, TrailingLogs=10 versus a large control, an idle cluster with one write per 250ms sample, and a 3s observation window.

The follower's own commit index was never advanced by the install path (recorded as 0 while its applied index was 83); the account treats this as an advertised-state inconsistency and does not treat it as an independent defect.
The vote-side consequence of the stale claim is source-derived (knowledge-1) and unmeasured: no election was induced while the victim held the claim.
The monotonic-store variant, other TrailingLogs values, larger clusters and longer windows are unmeasured; the receipt only shows no repair within the measured window.

scope.description: Two real three-voter cluster histories in one process, unchanged from the first run: a leader is isolated and appends entries that never reach a quorum, is shut down, and the remaining voters elect a leader, commit further entries and take a snapshot; the isolated node is then restarted on its unchanged in-memory log store and reconnected. In the trimmed case the leader's store is compacted to TrailingLogs=10 so only the snapshot can repair the follower; in the control TrailingLogs is large so entries repair it. Each case samples the victim's restores, applied index, commit index, cached last log entry, last snapshot and store range, plus the cluster frontier, for a 3s window with steady new writes.
assumptions: Fault model: no message loss inside the injected transport; the only induced event is a full transport partition of one voter plus its clean shutdown and restart on the same stores.

Reused facilities: MakeClusterCustom/MakeClusterOpts with inmemConfig timings, InmemStore, FileSnapshotStore, InmemTransport, MockFSM wrapped by a counting Restore, and the NewRaft restart pattern used by TestRaft_SnapshotRestore_Progress.
The victim's orphan suffix is produced by real Apply calls it accepted as leader while partitioned and is preserved because the restarted node replays its real log store.

Teardown now disconnects the victim after the measured window and waits with a bounded timeout instead of the stock cluster helper's panic-on-timeout path; this runs after every sampled value is recorded and does not affect the measurements.
excluded: No production logic was modified; the harness only adds a test file.
Automatic snapshotting is disabled (SnapshotThreshold huge, SnapshotInterval 1h) so the leader's snapshot index is controlled by the explicit Snapshot() call.

experiment.prefix: The harness builds the cluster with MakeClusterCustom (counting FSM), commits 60 entries, partitions the leader with c.Partition, fires 60 applies on it so they are appended locally without a quorum, waits for it to step down, shuts it down with Shutdown().Error(), waits for one of the remaining voters to be the only stable leader, commits 20 further entries, forces Snapshot(), records the snapshot and the trimmed store range, restarts the victim with NewRaft on its original stores and a fresh InmemTransport, reconnects it to both other transports, emits ca_setup carrying tag plus the premise fields, waits until the victim's applied index reaches the snapshot index, then samples every 250ms for 3s while applying one entry per sample on whichever node is leader, emits ca_probe with the raw values and derived booleans, and finally disconnects the victim before bounded teardown.
experiment.requirement: A follower that reinstalls the leader's snapshot must remain able to accept subsequent log entries from that leader, or its cached log state must not claim entries the snapshot superseded.

comparisons.description: Trimmed case: the follower's FSM was restored again after the first install, i.e. the same snapshot index was re-shipped during the window, while the leader's snapshot index is unchanged.
Trimmed case progress predicate: after the window the follower's applied index is still below the cluster frontier even though new entries committed and were applied elsewhere.
Trimmed case: the follower's cached last log index is still at or beyond the installed snapshot index with a lower term, and its store still holds that suffix.
Control: with an untrimmed leader log no snapshot is installed, separating the trigger from the existence of a stale suffix.
Control: the same cluster history without log trimming is repaired by log entries alone and the follower reaches the cluster frontier.

experiment.revision_reason: The first run's comparisons all resolved unknown because the admission event ca_setup omitted the mode field `tag` used by the trimmed_setup/untrimmed_setup alias conditions, so no admission could be associated; teardown could also race the leader's long-running InstallSnapshot RPC and panic the stock cluster helper. The harness now emits tag in ca_setup and tears down with a bounded wait after disconnecting the victim. Scenario, stores, comparisons, assertions, anchors and test selection are unchanged.
semantic_changes: ca_setup now emits tag ('trimmed'/'untrimmed') so the prerequisite alias conditions can associate the admission event with the measured ca_probe.
Teardown disconnects the victim after the measured window and waits with a bounded timeout instead of the stock cluster helper's panic-on-timeout path.
